rows.abstract: Aims to inspire debtors and their creditors to mutually and accurately resolve opposing claims and property rights and to guarantee a timely, fair, transparent, effective, and efficient rehabilitation or liquidation of debtors. AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 61 OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160,
OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract:
Proposes amendments based on the concept of devolution, where a component city is within the administrative and disciplinary jurisdiction of the province where it is geographically located.
States that a verified administrative complaint against any erring elective official shall be prepared as follows:
(a)  A complaint against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city (,) OR an independent component city (or component city) shall be filed before the Office of the President;
(b) A complaint against any elective official of a COMPONENT CITY OR municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President . . .

10912, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONTINUING
PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACT OF 2016
rows.abstract:
Redefines the term CPD Credit Unit to include PROFESSIONAL WORK EXPERIENCE to the value of an amount of learning that can be transferred to a qualification achieved . . .; Also redefines the term Quality Assurance to include INFORMAL, SAFE-DIRECTED, AND WORK-PLACE BASED LEARNING . . ., and Defines several terminologies among others such as competency, portability, recognition of prior learning, professional work experience, and specialty training.
Proposes several amendments regarding the following:  a) upgrading of qualifications toward career progression and specialization; b) appropriating qualification title attained based on PQF qualification level; c) professionals who were covered by mutual recognition agreements (MRAs); d) qualification assessment standards for every level of qualification or standards of practice indicated in their respective career progression and specialization; e) DOLE to coordinate and undertake the updating and revision of concerned private entities; f) qualification title under their respective career progression and specialization program to be included in the Phil. Standard & Occupational Classification (PSOC) and the Index of Occupational Services (IOS), position titles and salary grades of the Position Classification and Compensation System of the Government; g) provision regarding OFWs professionals.

rows.author: K095;
rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A WAGE EMPLOYMENT ASSISTANCE PROGRAM FOR DISPLACED
AND/OR VULNERABLEWORKERS INSTITUTIONALIZING FOR THE PURPOSE THE
TULONG PANGHANAPBUHAY SA ATING DISADVANTAGE/DISPLACED WORKERS
(TUPAD) PROGRAM OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT,
APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Describes TUPAD as a community-based package of assistance that provides for a short-term emergency employment program for displaced, underemployed, and seasonal workers; a program that acts as a social safety net to assist displaced or vulnerable workers in the informal economy, providing them wage employment to mitigate the impact of calamities, disasters, and epidemics on their livelihoods.
Aims to institutionalize the TUPAD program as a post-COVID intervention measure to help informal sector workers recover from economic displacement and loss of income due to enhanced community quarantine (ECQ) - whereby the DOLE is authorized to implement, motu propio employment projects in cases of massive displacements, define the eligibility of the qualified beneficiaries, and ensure the payment of at least a minimum wage rate for non-agricultural workers, among others.

OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “CONSUMER ACT OF THE
PHILIPPINES”, INCREASING ITS PENALTIES, AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to increase penalties to any person who shall violate any provision of Article 18 regarding the following consumer products concerns:  a) safety and quality standards including performance or use-oriented standards, codes of practice and methods of tests; b) products quality evaluation including safety, performance and comparative utility; c) associated unreasonable risks of injury to the public; d) research on quality improvement and investigation into causes and prevention of product related deaths, illness and injuries; and e) to assure the consistency of standardized products.
Proposes further the increase of penalties for any unlawful acts related to consumer products:  those that are not in conformity with and applicable quality or safety standard promulgated in this Act; those which has been declared as banned by a rule in this Act; those relating to notifications of substantial product hazards and to recall, repair, replace or refund unsafe products; and compliance with rule of prohibiting stockpiling.

rows.abstract:
Seeks to streamline all administrative procedures for the registration of patents, trademarks, and copyrights; to liberalize the registration on the transfer of technology; and enhance the enforcement of intellectual property rights. 
Proposes, among others, amendments to the following: the duration of the period when a certificate of registration shall remain in force and its renewal period; the sale or lease of an original work of painting or sculpture or the original manuscript of a writer or composer; and the corresponding penalties for infringement, and others.
